The client has given **three different/inconsistent accounts** of the accident mechanism. [note:2997036983] [note:2997038828] [note:2997037613]

The three accounts identified are: **(1)** the Metro-North vehicle merged into his lane and struck him, **(2)** both vehicles were merging and his own vehicle struck the other, and **(3)** he was sideswiped by a truck and then struck the sidewalk. [note:2997036983] [note:2997038828]

Yes, the strongest record says he was on duty: Metro-North’s IR-1 incident report for the 4/23/2023 8:30 a.m. crash has the “On-Duty” box checked for Anthony Ferrara and says he was “heading to the jobsite.” [doc:21122773658#p3]

That said, the broader scope-of-employment issue has not been fully resolved in discovery: Claims Service Bureau would not take a position when asked whether Metro-North accepted Ferrara was acting within the scope of employment, and counsel noted the vehicle assignment/dispatch records were still sought as the contemporaneous proof of whether he was on duty that morning. [call:5029638323] [note:2997038048]

Bottom line: there is affirmative Metro-North incident-report evidence that Ferrara was on duty, but Metro-North/CSB has not formally accepted scope of employment in the cited materials. [doc:21122773658#p3] [call:5029638323]

Kyle Pullano is a Metro-North employee identified as the person who can answer whether Anthony Ferrara was within the scope of employment/on duty at the time of the collision. [note:2997037058]

Dr. Hostin diagnosed neck, mid-back, low-back, bilateral shoulder, bilateral elbow, bilateral knee, and bilateral wrist sprains as resolved. [doc:21122792168#p11]

He opined that Mr. Sapini’s condition had plateaued and was medically stationary. [doc:21122792168#p11]

He found the subjective complaints did not correlate with radiographic or other objective findings. [doc:21122792168#p11]

He stated lumbar range-of-motion limitations appeared only on direct testing, while transfers and ambulation showed no dysfunction or restriction. [doc:21122792168#p11]

He stated the shoulder and knee range-of-motion deficits were not associated with objective pathology, and he attributed them to subjective pain concerns with significant guarding. [doc:21122792168#p12]

He noted a positive Tinel’s over the left cubital tunnel indicating ulnar nerve irritability, but said there were no complaints consistent with ulnar neuritis and no treatment was indicated. [doc:21122792168#p12]

He concluded Mr. Sapini could return to work without restrictions. [doc:21122792168#p12]

Dr. Jack W. Tsao, the defense neurology expert, diagnosed Justin Sapini as status post traumatic brain injury, status post post-concussion syndrome, and status post post-traumatic headaches/migraines, all “objectively resolved.” [doc:21122791073#p6]

He also opined that Sapini could work and perform daily activities without restrictions. [doc:21122791073#p6]

Related defense radiology review was consistent with that position: Dr. Katzman found the 08/08/2023 brain MRI normal, with no evidence of traumatic brain injury, hemorrhage, contusion, or posttraumatic encephalomalacia. [doc:21122790428#p7]

The defense radiology review was by Dr. Marc J. Katzman, M.D., and was served as an expert radiology report concerning Justin Sapini’s MRIs and other imaging. [doc:21122790428#p3] [doc:21122790428#p1]

Dr. Katzman repeatedly opined that the imaging studies showed no traumatic injury related to the claimed accident. [doc:21122790428#p3]

For the 08/08/2023 brain MRI, he found no traumatic brain injury, hemorrhage, contusion, or posttraumatic encephalomalacia, and called the examination normal. [doc:21122790428#p7]

For the 08/08/2023 DTI brain study, he found the study within normal limits with no significant white-matter microstructural disruption. [doc:21122790428#p7]

For the 08/08/2023 NeuroQuant analysis, he found no age-disproportionate or post-traumatic brain atrophy. [doc:21122790428#p7]

For the 07/03/2023 knee MRIs, he found no recent traumatic right or left knee injury or internal derangement. [doc:21122790428#p3] [doc:21122790428#p4]

For the 05/24/2023 right shoulder MRI, he found no evidence of recent traumatic right shoulder injury and called the exam unremarkable. [doc:21122790428#p5]

For the 09/10/2018 chest x-ray, he found no acute chest findings and noted that the exam predated the 04/23/2023 accident. [doc:21122790428#p6]

This conflicts with plaintiff-side imaging that reported abnormal DTI findings, a hemosiderin focus, and a positive predictive value for traumatic brain injury greater than 95%. [doc:21122777513#p7] [doc:21122790428#p7]

Kim’s bottom line was that neither side is obstructing, but both sides are slow. [note:2997038543]

Defendants pleaded these affirmative defenses:

- Plaintiff’s culpable conduct/comparative negligence and assumption of risk, including reckless or negligent operation, failure to keep a proper lookout, speeding, failure to control the vehicle, failure to keep distance, failure to signal or use the horn, and failure to avoid the accident. [doc:21122771228#p1]
- Seat-belt defense: plaintiff failed to use an available seat belt, causing, exacerbating, or contributing to the claimed damages. [doc:21122771228#p2]
- Serious-injury threshold: defendants objected that plaintiff bears the burden to prove a serious injury under New York Insurance Law. [doc:21122771228#p2]
- Failure to mitigate damages, including refusal or failure to seek timely/proper medical care, follow medical advice, comply with instructions, or otherwise take steps to recover. [doc:21122771228#p2]
- Collateral source offset under CPLR 4545(c) for medical care, rehabilitative services, lost earnings, or other economic loss replaced or indemnified from collateral sources. [doc:21122771228#p2]
- Emergency doctrine: defendants claimed a sudden event they did not cause or contribute to. [doc:21122771228#p3]
